scenarios: The real first purchase opens the selected owned Cinder Machine Shop, identifies its stable owned ID and reports pristine repair status
A normal-frame stock test supplies an actual measured baseline; the confirmed engine fitting deducts exactly 270 credits on the same owned car
The purchased engine changes normal-frame accepted acceleration; a native v7 download records that exact source, build, command tape and measured terminal result
All four actual stock/current/proposed benchmark receipts return to the Garage and are explicitly re-simulated before measured comparison display; verification preserves the save
Every named mechanical/paint section fits real existing catalogue parts and quantized settings through explicit transactions; exact owned identity and pristine condition survive all nine categories
Native JSON export/import, browser reload and responsive named-section navigation preserve every installed part, setting, credit and owned identity

The standalone v7 viewer reconstructs the original engine-only build after the live car has different parts/paint; play, pause, midpoint/end seek, camera, reduced motion and restart reproduce its accepted result without touching the save
The actual browser WebGL context can be lost/restored while the viewer preserves its reconstructed build and paused accepted tick
Native file admission rejects a different source, tampered recipe identity, fictional result and diagnostic receipt; no rejected file can start playback or mutate ownership
Historical Replay Theatre rejects the separate v7 contract rather than reinterpreting it as a published v2–v6 recording
A real second-tab paid paint refit cancels an in-flight evidence reconstruction; CONFLICT keeps Verify disabled and results empty until explicit Reload and a fresh verification
